Section 02
Problem Research
Threat framing · category difference · user validation

Enterprise agents are using third-party capabilities without a trust layer

Input Surface
Third-party skills and MCP tools enter the agent workflow.
Declared Intent
What the extension says it will do is often easier to approve than what it can actually trigger.
Enterprise Agent Runtime
Once installed, extensions can influence a much broader operating surface.
File Access
Network Access
Tool Invocation
Observed Behavior
Actual runtime behavior may drift after approval.
→
Risk
Security exposure, weak accountability, and poor traceability.
The governance gap is simple, but operationally serious.
Enterprise agents increasingly depend on external skills and MCP tools to move faster. That dependency creates a new trust problem that most teams cannot currently govern well.
High-impact permissions: third-party extensions can influence file access, network access, and tool invocation.
Low installation visibility: teams often cannot explain what was approved, by whom, or whether it later changed.
Weak incident traceability: when behavior drifts, organizations struggle to prove what happened after the fact.

Why agent extensions are different from ordinary software packages

Dimension Ordinary package review Agent extension trust problem
Declared purpose Usually inferred from code, version history, and dependency metadata. Must also consider descriptions, capability declarations, and behavior claimed to the agent.
Effective permissions Often constrained by runtime or service boundaries. May inherit broader file, network, or tool influence from the agent environment.
Risk timing Risk is often visible at install or build time. Risk may emerge later through delayed or behavior-drift actions after approval.
Control model Static scanning and dependency checks may be enough for first review. Requires static checks, trust signals, runtime enforcement, and auditability together.
Governance question "Is this package safe enough to pull?" "Should this extension be installed, trusted now, allowed to run, and explainable later?"

Who has this problem?

Alex: enterprise agent security lead
Needs visibility, control, and defensible governance
Alex needs a way to answer what is installed, what is risky, what was blocked, and how to explain a security event to management or audit stakeholders.
What Alex values: clear install decisions, runtime controls, and traceable evidence after an incident.
Why this matters: without a trust layer, every third-party extension increases uncertainty rather than capability.
Ray: agent developer under time pressure
Needs a fast decision, not a long report
Ray wants to know in seconds whether a skill should be installed, sandboxed, or blocked, without waiting for a heavyweight security process.
Lightweight validation: the project is grounded in a real classroom MVP and a concrete developer workflow rather than an abstract policy idea.
Design implication: every result must be explainable enough for Alex and fast enough for Ray.
Section 03
Product Solution
Architecture · control logic · MVP scope

Product Definition

AgentGuard is a trust layer for the AI agent supply chain, covering everything including skills, MCP tools, dependencies. Instead of a one-time check, we manage risk across the full lifecycle — before installation, during installation, and at runtime.
Defense Principles
Principle 1
Zero Trust Architecture
Never trust, always verify every third-party skill before and after installation.
Principle 2
Principle of Least Privilege
Strict validation of minimal permission requirements. No skill gets more access than declared.
Principle 3
Full-Stack Traceability
Maintaining a verifiable audit trail for every runtime action. Explainable evidence, not just verdicts.

Supply-Chain Ingestion
OpenClaw Skill Source Code

Dependency Auditor
Checks different types of files · package.json. · requirements.txt. · ClawHavoc-style dependency lockfiles
3-Layer Deep Defense Engine
1
Pre-install Static Analysis
Before any installation, we scan for code, permissions, APIs and risky dependencies. If there were anything suspicious, We will take a clear action.
suspicious patterns declared permissions sensitive API refs risky dependencies risk level & evaluation
Output → risk level, explanation, clear action: allow, block, or deny not just a score
2
Install-time Trust Verification & Sandbox
Verify whether the component is trustworthy now. For anything looks risky, we send it to sandbox simulation.
trust verification sandbox simulation hash lock change tracking source & maintainer metadata
Output → proceed to install or halt pipeline
3
Runtime Behavior Monitor
Continuously observe file access attempts, network requests, sensitive tool calls, If behavior departs from what was declared, we can immediately block or isolate it in real time.
file access network egress sensitive calls fuse & isolate cleartext evidence
Output → risk score, recommended action, audit trail

Real-time Interception Log
Logs intercepted events with risk score, evidence, and recommended action for transparency.

Section 04
UX / Demo
Live demo · product UX · visible reasoning

Product UX — one product, four outcomes

1
Benign
Green path through static, sandbox, trust, and runtime layers.
▶
2
Static Block
Undeclared file access and risky signature are stopped before installation.
▶
3
Sandbox Block
Suspicious outbound behavior is detected during detonation.
▶
4
Runtime Block
Delayed behavior triggers the runtime fuse after installation age is simulated.
The UX is designed for two audiences at once.
1
Fast judgment: developers need a decision in seconds, not a long compliance report.
2
Visible reasoning: every blocked outcome is paired with stage-specific evidence and an operator-readable explanation.
3
Low-friction safe paths: the goal is not to stop all third-party use, but to make trusted adoption manageable.
4
Dashboard value: security leads see what is installed, what is risky, and what has already been contained.

Business model — what the core product ladder looks like

Free Developer Scanner
Adoption & Education
  • Limited installations and static scans for individual developers
  • Creates awareness while teaching users what "safe installation" means
  • Supports product-led discovery without a heavy sales motion
Team Tier
Visibility & Monitoring
  • Shared dashboard, unlimited scanning, and basic monitoring
  • Re-scan triggers and lightweight review flows for growing teams
  • Natural upgrade point once multiple agents or operators are involved
Enterprise Tier
Control & Auditability
  • Advanced policies, runtime control, private deployment, and dedicated support
  • Audit exports and incident evidence for governance stakeholders
  • Supports enterprise buying triggers such as compliance and internal security review
What are the core offerings and who are they for?

GTM Path & Closing
Adoption path · channels · final claim

GTM Strategy — Product-Led Growth (PLG)

Build Awareness
Action: Launch a free Developer Edition with limited scan credits.
Goal: Attract the developer community and establish initial word-of-mouth in technical circles.
Convert Teams
Action: Introduce a Team Edition with visual dashboards and basic monitoring.
Goal: Meet core team collaboration needs and achieve initial conversion from individual users to teams.
Win Enterprises
Action: Release an Enterprise Edition with SSO integration, audit exports, and private deployment.
Goal: Serve large enterprise clients and unlock scalable commercial value across the full lifecycle.
PLG Framework
From Individual Developers to Enterprise Clients, a Scalable Growth Journey.
